answer: Picture honest agents gathered on an open knoll where every identity must post a refundable bond before it can act. Peers spend quadratically-priced challenge credits to flag suspected fakes: each extra accusation aimed at one cluster costs the square of the last, so probing a sybil swarm of N identities folds cost inward like a lotus. A confirmed fake forfeits its bond, split among the accurate challengers. A farm thus pays N bonds up front, and like the tight meter of a sonnet, every line it adds only clenches the trap harder; honest bonds return in full.
